newsitem.title: CROATIA: Zagreb teachers stage quiet protest over wages.
newsitem.headline: Zagreb teachers stage quiet protest over wages.

text.p: Some 1,000 public service employees, including school and university teachers, marched through Zagreb on Wednesday in protest at the government's failure to meet their demands for a fifty percent pay rise.
Banners read: "Your children are taught by paupers", and "We are worse off every year".
The protesters were blocked by police from gathering in front of the national parliament building. They had wanted to address the government, but lit candles instead.
The crowd dispersed peacefully after half an hour, when its representatives were told by the parliamentary speaker to raise the salary issue at a regular session.

Public sector trade unions called for the resignation of Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa for allegedly not respecting previously reached agreements that would include an increase of wages, which now average some $220 a month.
The event was the latest in a series of social protests that have shaken the capital since last week.
